Urea is the main thing in urine that the kidneys need to remove from your body. It is a product of the breakdown of protein. Remember that your cells are constantly dying and growing so there is lots of protein digestion happening even if you aren't eating meat. Urea is chemically very similar to ammonia and in fact if it sits too long it becomes ammonia. That's why pee smells almost sweet at first but if you don't flush it for a bit it smells like ammonia. Urea therefore has a very low pH which is very bad for your cells and it can kill them. For this reason the body removes all urea top priority (and uric acid from breakdown of DNA but in trace amounts). Because of the pH it's important to dilute it in the kidneys so that it doesn't "burn" your ureters, bladder, and urethra. Your kidneys will take that water whether you have it to spare or not. If you were dehydrated and crawling through the desert, you would still produce urine. That water in your pee comes directly out of your blood vessels. It's clear because the Red blood cells can't fit through the filters in the kidney, called glomeruli. When your blood loses water and gets thick, it pulls in more water from your cells. So if you don't drink enough water, your pee burns you, your blood gets thick, and your cells shrivel. So try to pee clear.
